judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard all-caps claims-made legend; each operative term ('first made', 'reported in writing ... pursuant to the terms herein') is defined or cross-referenced elsewhere, so the legend itself supplies little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks Insuring Agreement I (c004) and Section V.A (c036), though V.A's closing sentence limits coverage to Claims 'first made during the Policy Period' and omits the Extended Reporting Period the legend mentions — a minor slack rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence countersignature condition; 'shall not be valid unless also signed by another duly authorized representative' is a bright-line condition, not an ambiguous one, though it can be argued about if a countersignature is missing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere (including VIII.K Alteration and Assignment, c053, which also requires an authorized representative's signature) contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate consideration and reliance recital; 'all Statements made in the Application and all information provided to the Insurer' is broad but the Application is separately defined in III.A.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restates the reliance premise of VIII.B (c044), but VIII.B adds a severability regime that qualifies the unqualified reliance recited here — a recital-versus-operative tension of modest size.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant is garbled ('made against any Insured by or on behaif Employee' omits words), and the reporting condition couples an elastic 'as soon as practicable after any Insured first becomes aware' with a hard 60-day outer limit — both are classic points of construction in claims-made coverage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the Section III.D definition of Claim (c011), the awareness/notice provisions in VI (c039–c041, which set a differently-triggered 60-day clock) and V.A's deemed-one-Claim relation-back (c036); those interlocking triggers are where a which-policy-responds dispute lives.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A carefully bounded spousal extension with an express carve-out for the spouse's own wrongful acts and a defined reach for 'spouse'; little is left open on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the definitions of Insured Individual (c017) and Loss (c019) without visible friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short, enumerated extension to estates, heirs, representatives and assigns, with an express exclusion for their own wrongful acts; the terms are conventional and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Bankruptcy condition (c051) and the Insured Individual definition (c017); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger is written narrowly — 'if the Insurer chooses not to renew or the Parent Company cancels' — and the election clock runs from 'the effective date of cancellation, or nonrenewal', a date the policy never fixes for nonrenewal.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cancellation/Nonrenewal (c045) also permits the Insurer to cancel for nonpayment, a route this ERP trigger does not mention, and the Authorization Clause (c052) carves ERP notice out of the Parent Company's agency, leaving who may elect somewhat unsettled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition piles up general catch-alls — 'any other such documents submitted in connection with the underwriting', policies 'of which this policy is a renewal, replacement or which succeed it in time' — whose outer boundary is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds the reliance clauses in the Preamble (c003) and VIII.B (c044), which incorporate 'all such statements' as part of the Policy; the breadth interacts with, but does not contradict, those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any other payment to or for the benefit of an employee arising out of the employment relationship' is a wide catch-all after specifics, though the closing sentence expressly subtracts salary, wages and commissions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is used in the Loss carve-outs (c019.4, .6) and Exclusion B.1 (c035), which pull in the same direction; no inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One line covering 'any oral, written or implied' employment contract — broad, but the breadth is deliberate and the terms are ordinary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion A.4 and Exclusion B.3 (c034, c035) cut back contract-based recovery to express written contracts, so coverage granted through this definition is largely retracted downstream — a tension worth noting but a familiar insuring-agreement/exclusion structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Everything turns on 'a written demand against any Insured for monetary or non-monetary relief' — whether a lawyer's letter, an internal grievance or an EEOC charge is a 'demand' is exactly the kind of boundary two parties read differently, and the four enumerated species plus the collective-bargaining carve-out invite expressio unius arguments.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits directly against the definition of Potential Claim (c025), which covers an 'allegation or accusation ... provided such allegation does not constitute a Claim', and against the first-made/reporting machinery in I (c004), V.A (c036) and VI.A (c039); in a dispute over which of two successive policy years responds, those provisions cannot be applied without deciding when a writing crossed from allegation to demand.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable and necessary legal fees and expenses' is an open standard, and the parenthetical excluding Insureds' own compensation and overhead draws a line that is easy to argue about at the margin.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with V.C's consent requirement and V.A's erosion of the Limit (c036, c038) and with Exclusion B's defense-costs-only regime (c035); those provisions are aligned rather than in conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence keyed to 'the violation of any Federal, State, or local statute, regulation, ordinance or common law concerning discrimination in employment' — broad but bounded by external law.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds Wrongful Employment Act (c031) and is carved around by Exclusion A.5 (c034); the pieces harmonise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list is broad and the fifth item's 'solely for or on behalf of the Policyholder' limitation is a genuine boundary question for contractors; item 1 ('duly appointed officer') is also grammatically mismatched with the plural lead-in.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Employee' overlaps heavily with 'Insured Individual' (c017) yet the two definitions differ on leased persons and contractors, and Insuring Agreement A covers claims made 'by or on behalf [of an] Employee' while Third Party Claim (c029) expressly excludes independent contractors — an overlap a coverage fight could exploit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: After two specific sexual-harassment limbs the definition closes with 'illegal work related harassment', a general catch-all against enumerated specifics whose reach is precisely the ejusdem generis problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere contradicts it; it feeds Wrongful Employment Act (c031) as one of the listed torts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure definitional identity — 'Insured means the Insured Individuals and the Policyholder' — with nothing to construe on its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both components are separately defined (c017, c022) and used consistently throughout; no friction located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The five limbs are conventional, though limbs 4 and 5 turn on a written indemnity agreement 'prior to any Claim', a condition whose timing can be disputed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps and partly conflicts in scope with the 'Employee' definition (c014) — the same leased or contracted person can be an Employee but not an Insured Individual — which matters for who can sue and who is covered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Common nexus [of] any fact, circumstance, situation, event, transaction, cause or series of causally or logically connected' facts is famously elastic — 'logically connected' has no natural stopping point and is regularly the term parties fight over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It powers the deemed-one-Claim relation-back in V.A (c036) and the prior/pending exclusion A.2(b) (c034), so its breadth directly determines which policy year responds — the live question in a successive-policy dispute.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long, carefully enumerated definition; the soft spots are 'matters uninsurable under the law applicable to this Policy' and the choice-of-law rule for punitive damages, but the drafting is otherwise tight.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-outs mesh with Exclusion B (c035) and the Punitive Damages definition (c026) and Item 6 of the Declarations; no contradiction surfaced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Six enumerated torts (with a duplicated numeral in the text) closed by a predicate limiting them to Claims 'alleged as part of' another covered wrong — the 'as part of' link is the arguable phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The tail predicate ties it to Breach of Employment Contract, Discrimination, Harassment, Retaliation and Wrongful Job Action (c010, c013, c015, c027, c032), and Exclusion A.8 (c034) carves emotional distress back in; the pieces largely cohere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pointer to Item 1 of the Declarations, which names FINRA; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in Policyholder (c022), Cancellation (c045) and the Authorization Clause (c052).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite: Parent Company plus Subsidiaries, including debtor-in-possession status.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the Subsidiary definition (c028) and Section VIII.A (c043), whose acquisition thresholds are themselves murky, but the definition itself does not conflict with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is one line but its cross-reference is wrong: it makes Policy Period 'subject to prior termination in accordance with Section VII.C', and Section VII is Notices — the cancellation provision is Section VIII.C.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The misdirection has to be repaired by reading it against VIII.C Cancellation/Nonrenewal (c045), which does state that the Policy Period ends at the effective time of cancellation; the error is correctable but is a genuine mechanical defect in the instrument's internal wiring.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any substance ... exhibiting any hazardous characteristics' followed by an open-ended 'without limitation' list and a further 'shall also mean' catch-all covering noise and electromagnetic fields is a textbook general-versus-specific scope problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is used only in Exclusion A.7 (c034), which carves back Retaliation claims; nothing elsewhere pulls against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'An allegation or accusation ... provided such allegation does not constitute a Claim, but subsequently may give rise to a Claim' is defined negatively against Claim, so its boundary is only as clear as that other definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits in direct dependence on III.D Claim (c011) and drives the Awareness Provision VI.A relation-back (c039); if a writing is characterised as a demand rather than an allegation the two provisions send the claim to different policy years.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed definition naming three statutes' liquidated damages; the drafting is specific and leaves little play.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with Loss item 9 and the most-favourable-jurisdiction proviso (c019) and Item 6 of the Declarations (coverage 'Yes'); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Illegal retaliatory treatment of Employees, including any retaliatory treatment for ...' uses 'including' before four specifics, leaving the general opener to do the work — modestly open but tethered to illegality.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Retaliation is the carve-back in Exclusions A.5 and A.7 (c034), so its scope determines how much those exclusions retain; the provisions are aligned in direction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trailing clause — 'on or before the effective date of this Policy, or after the effective date of this Policy if the entity is covered pursuant to Section VIII.A.1, solely with regard to Wrongful Acts occurring at or after the time such entity became a Subsidiary' — is syntactically tangled and its temporal reach is not obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on VIII.A.1 (c043), whose ten-percent and hundred-and-ten-percent employee thresholds are themselves confusingly drafted, so the two must be read together to know who is a Subsidiary at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any natural person who is, or attempted to be, a customer or vendor' is odd phrasing, and the closing exclusion of independent contractors' claims is a specific carve-out from an otherwise broad class.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Independent contractors can be Employees and Insured Individuals under c014 and c017 yet are barred from bringing Third Party Claims here, and Exclusion A.9 (c034) separately bars contractor contract claims — a set of overlapping treatments of the same persons.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line umbrella definition joining two defined terms; nothing intrinsic to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both components are defined at c031 and c033 and used consistently in Insuring Agreement I and the exclusions.
